methodological_rigor.justification: Combines TCGA-GTEx and GEO (GSE9891) bioinformatics analyses with siRNA-based knockdown in A2780 and OVCAR3 cells, supported by 15 normal and 30 EOC clinical specimens. Standard tools (DESeq2, WGCNA, GEPIA2, oncoPredict, ssGSEA) are applied appropriately. However, there is no animal/in vivo validation, experiments are reported as only 2-3 independent repeats, only two cell lines are used, and rescue experiments to confirm EMT-pathway dependency are absent. Thresholds (e.g., adjusted p < 1e-32 for DEGs) are unusually stringent and inconsistently applied. Knockdown efficiencies of 55-61% are modest.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Findings identify NCAPG2 as a potentially actionable oncogene in EOC associated with EMT and chemoresistance, with plausible but entirely preclinical translational implications. No in vivo model, no functional link to clinical outcomes in a prospective cohort, and drug-sensitivity inferences are based on oncoPredict modeling rather than experimental validation. This is a preclinical bioinformatics + in vitro study, Oxford LoE 5.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods sections describe databases, software versions, antibody dilutions, cell culture conditions, and statistical tests in reasonable detail. However, there is no animal work so ARRIVE is tangential, no explicit preclinical reporting checklist is cited, primer and siRNA sequences are in supplementary tables not shown, and the clinical specimen cohort lacks STROBE-style demographic reporting. The Results section is placed after the Discussion under "Additional Sections", which is unusual. No code or processed data deposit is stated.

novelty_literature.justification: NCAPG2's oncogenic role has been characterized in HCC, glioblastoma, lung adenocarcinoma, melanoma, and pan-cancer and pancreatic cancer studies (refs 15-18, 39), so the central finding is an extension to EOC rather than a first-in-class discovery. The integrative framing (expression, immune infiltration, DDR/chemoresistance correlation, in vitro EMT mechanism) adds incremental scope, but the individual analyses are standard in this genre.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable with a logical narrative, but exhibits translation-quality issues ("collectin II complex" instead of condensin II, "different expression analysis", duplicated sentences). The structural placement of Results under "Additional Sections" after Discussion disrupts normal flow. Figures are described in depth and numerical reporting (R values, p-values, knockdown efficiencies) is explicit.

key_strengths: Integrates TCGA-GTEx, GEO, and clinical samples with in vitro knockdown experiments in two EOC cell lines
Multi-angle functional characterization including DDR gene correlations, chemoresistance gene correlations, and immune infiltration signatures
EMT mechanism supported by concordant Western blot evidence for E-cadherin upregulation and N-cadherin/Vimentin downregulation
Clinical tissue qRT-PCR confirms elevated NCAPG2 in advanced (FIGO III-IV) versus early (I-II) disease
key_concerns: No in vivo validation; mechanistic claims about EMT and chemoresistance rest on correlative bioinformatics and 2-cell-line in vitro data
NCAPG2 oncogenic role already reported in multiple cancers including pan-cancer analyses, limiting novelty
Knockdown efficiency of 55-61% is modest and no rescue experiments confirm pathway specificity
Drug sensitivity predictions rely on oncoPredict modeling rather than experimental drug treatment
Results placed after Discussion under "Additional Sections"; translation-quality errors (e.g., "collectin II complex") and missing code/data availability
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent integrative preclinical study that extends NCAPG2's oncogenic role to EOC but with limited novelty and without in vivo validation; mid-tier oncology journal after major revisions is appropriate.
